Sanjeev Singh Sahni, Xometry’s current President, will succeed Altschuler as Chief Executive Officer and join the Board of Directors.

After more than a decade of building the Xometry business, I have decided to transition from my role as CEO into the Executive Chairman of the Board, effective July 1. I am thrilled to announce that Sanjeev Singh Sahni will become Xometry’s next CEO. Since joining as President, Sanjeev has been my close partner in shaping Xometry’s direction. His transition to CEO represents a natural and steady next step as Xometry’s revenue growth and profitability continue to accelerate. It has been the privilege of my career to lead this incredible company. When we first started in 2013, the mission was to fundamentally digitize the massive custom manufacturing market. And because of our team’s dedication, we have made tremendous progress scaling our marketplace and delivering the record-breaking results we shared in our earnings press release today. In my new role as Executive Chairman, I will remain deeply involved in the company’s future, focusing on strategic growth initiatives and key corporate partnerships. In short, I am not going anywhere. I look forward to supporting Sanjeev and the entire executive team as we increase our momentum. You can read more in today’s press release https://lnkd.in/e58xSAHc

results.title: AMENDMENT TO EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT - RealDealDocs
highlights:
This SEC filing details an amendment to the employment agreement between Xometry, Inc. and Sanjeev Singh Sahni, effective July 1, 2026. Under this amendment, Sahni will transition to the role of Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and will also serve on the Company’s Board of Directors. His annual base salary will be set at $600,000, with the potential for an annual performance bonus of up to 100% of his base salary, contingent upon meeting performance goals established by the Board. The amendment also specifies that Sahni's eligibility for bonuses is dependent on his status as an employee in good standing at the time of payment. Significantly, the amendment modifies severance provisions, extending the severance pay period from twelve to eighteen months and introducing a cash payment equivalent to one-and-a-half times the target annual bonus upon termination. Additionally, Sahni is entitled to a one-time cash award of $400,000, payable in December 2026, subject to repayment if he resigns without good reason or is terminated for cause within twelve months of his CEO start date. The amendment also includes provisions for the grant of restricted stock units valued at $3.6 million, which will vest quarterly over five years, contingent on Sahni's continued employment. The amendment emphasizes that any changes to the terms require mutual written consent and maintains the integrity of the original employment agreement, with the amendment serving to modify rather than replace it.
